Thermo-responsive Ionizable Xanthone Bolaamphiphiles for Dynamic Self-Assembly into Nanovesicles Enabling Enhanced Intracellular Drug Release and Tumor Growth Inhibition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive supramolecular nanocarriers capable of controlled drug release have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional chemotherapy; however, the development of structurally defined small-molecule systems exhibiting thermo-responsive behavior within biologically relevant temperature ranges remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of ionizable xanthone-based bolaamphiphiles (X1–X3) engineered to undergo temperature-triggered self-assembly in aqueous media. Systematic modulation of oxyethylene-chain density revealed that X3 exhibits a sharp and reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transition within the physiological temperature window (35–40 °C), leading to the formation of stable nanovesicular assemblies. The resulting X3 nanovesicles accommodate doxorubicin (DOX) with an encapsulation efficiency of ∼25% and a drug-loading content of 11% while maintaining good colloidal stability under physiologically relevant conditions. X3-DOX nanovesicles exhibit progressive thermoresponsive drug release near physiological temperature, which is further enhanced under mild hyperthermia, together with an additional acid-responsive release behavior associated with protonation of the piperazine units (apparent pKa ≈ 4.5). Cellular studies performed in 4T1 breast cancer and A549 lung cancer cells demonstrated enhanced intracellular drug accumulation, superior cytotoxicity, and effective suppression of multicellular tumor spheroids compared with free DOX. Furthermore, the nanoformulation exhibited excellent hemocompatibility, favorable biodistribution characteristics, and efficient systemic clearance. In a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model, X3-DOX induced remarkable tumor-growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. These findings establish thermo-responsive xanthone-based nanovesicles as a versatile supramolecular platform for controlled anticancer drug delivery and provide a molecularly defined strategy for developing stimuli-responsive nanomedicines.

title: Robust Thermal Stability, Flame Retardancy, and Weather Resistance Cross-Linked Cellulose Aerogel toward High-Performance Passive Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The frequent occurrence of high temperatures has driven the development of green passive cooling technologies. Traditional passive radiative cooling materials have single performance, insufficient weather resistance and structural stability, and are unable to adapt to outdoor multifunctional thermal management. In this study, cellulose nanofibers were used as the substrate, and silica and methyltrimethoxysilane were incorporated to prepare a composite aerogel. Tests show that the optimal sample has excellent radiation cooling, heat insulation, flame retardancy, hydrophobicity, and sound absorption performance. With a solar reflectance of 93.5% and a mid-infrared emissivity of 94.3%, it provides a maximum outdoor temperature reduction of 15.7 °C. Its minimum thermal conductivity reaches 0.034 W m–1 K–1, offering excellent thermal insulation performance. The total heat release and the rate of heat release were significantly reduced, and flame retardancy was greatly improved. In addition, the sample exhibits a water contact angle of 137.2°, endowing it with favorable self-cleaning properties. The average sound absorption coefficient reaches 0.78 in the broadband range of 1000–6300 Hz, and the noise reduction performance is superior to that of commercial materials. This multifunctional composite aerogel overcomes the performance limitations of traditional materials and offers new insights into the development and application of outdoor integrated thermal management functional materials.

title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024–2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering.

title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl–amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation–decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl–amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models.

title: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) – a versatile and bio-based platform chemical
abstract: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) emerges as a versatile bio-based platform chemical, combining renewable accessibility, rich multifunctional reactivity, asymmetric synthesis potential, and routes to high-value chemicals and sustainable materials alike.

title: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell (Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells.

title: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution.

title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

title: Author Correction: In vivo mitochondrial base editing restores genotype and visual function in a mouse model of LHON

title: Transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization: a mechanistic view
abstract: Icosahedral carboranes have extensive applications owing to their unique properties. This review summarizes advances in the mechanistic study of transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization.

title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with—and is in some cases surpassed by—TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2-expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases.

title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual’s distress to one’s own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer’s position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer’s spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.

title: Nested economies of scale in global city mass
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    A long-standing puzzle in urban science is whether there is an intrinsic match between human populations and the mass of their built environments. Existing models assume proportionality: each additional resident demands the same amount of building material. Our analysis of more than 3,000 cities worldwide challenges this linear assumption. Built mass grows more slowly than population (that is, sublinear scaling), across cities (
                    β
                     = 0.90) and across neighborhoods within a city (
                    δ
                     = 0.75). This means that larger cities and denser neighborhoods achieve economies of scale with less per capita built mass. Our theoretical framework further shows that the across-city scaling pattern emerges from the uneven within-city distribution of people. These findings caution against well-meaning interventions, such as height and building-size limits, that artificially flatten cities’ natural density gradients. Effective urban policy should instead move beyond per capita linear thinking, adopting scale-adjusted metrics and managing cities as nested complex systems.

title: Urban scaling and the dynamics of individual cities
abstract: Cross-sectional urban scaling exponents do not describe how individual cities evolve over time. Using theory and empirical evidence, the authors show that scaling laws reflect statistical relationships among cities with heterogeneous trajectories, limiting their mechanistic interpretation and their use for policy at the level of individual cities.

title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses.

title: Metal–Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2–96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4–99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

title: Nerve activity initiates autoimmune hair loss
abstract: Understanding the triggers of autoimmunity might lead to better therapies, with hair loss among the conditions for which underpinning factors have come to light.

title: Are salaries getting worse? Many scientists think so
abstract: Nature’s survey of almost 4,000 researchers shows that you’re not alone if you struggle to make ends meet or your last pay rise is a distant memory.

title: Constructing Continuous Proton Channels through One-Dimensional Confined Nanofillers for High-Performance H2/O2 Fuel Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Establishing continuous proton transport pathways alongside robust interfacial interactions remains a critical bottleneck for organic–inorganic composite proton exchange membranes (PEMs). Herein, we report a rationally designed hybrid nanofiller (SUC@PHNTs) that integrates the long-range orientational order of one-dimensional (1D) halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) with the high-density proton-hopping sites of the metal-organic framework UiO-66-(COOH)2 (UC) and zwitterionic surface grafts. Subsequently when dispersed in a sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) matrix, this 1D confined architecture bridges discrete UC domains into interconnected, continuous proton-conducting channels, effectively reducing proton transport tortuosity. Specifically, the S/SUC@PHNTs-3.0% membrane delivered 174.72 mS cm–1 (80 °C, 100% RH), corresponding to a 35.21% increase relative to pristine SPEEK. In an H2/O2 single-cell test, the membrane delivered a maximum power density of 793.29 mW cm–2, substantially exceeding that of SPEEK. Moreover, the voltage decay rate over 150 h of continuous operation was merely 0.42 mV h–1, indicative of excellent long-term operational stability. Overall, these results establish that the 1D confined nanofiller design strategy provides a promising technological pathway toward high-performance PEMs.

title: Regulating the Activity and Product Selectivity of Electrocatalytic Glycerol Oxidation by Changing the Au Loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) has attracted much attention recently in the production of high-value-added chemicals coupled with water electrolysis for energy-saving hydrogen production due to its mild reaction conditions, green and harmless, and lower onset potential than the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis. However, under alkaline conditions, glycerol is prone to generate low-value-added C1 products, and the selectivity for C3 products is a significant challenge. In this work, we successfully regulated the activity and product selectivity of electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation by changing the Au loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF. The results showed that the selectivity of Au/Ni2.86Te2/NF-3 for glyceric acid (GLA) was 72.41%, and its GOR performance and selectivity were superior to those of recently reported catalysts. An appropriate Au loading results in favorable changes in Au distribution and surface electronic structure, which are associated with improved GOR activity and GLA selectivity.

title: 3D Printed Sandpile-Shaped Photothermal Evaporator Based on Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Efficient Water Evaporation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The interface evaporation technology driven by solar energy has received widespread attention due to its advantages of being clean, pollution-free, and low in energy consumption. However, the cumbersome preparation process of existing high-efficiency evaporators hinders their large-scale promotion and application. Furthermore, we find that the inclined slope of the sandpile has the geometric condition of “forced reflection,” and the incident light can form reciprocating reflection between adjacent sandpiles, greatly improving the light capture efficiency and providing a structural basis for achieving efficient evaporation. Inspired by this, we construct a sandpile-shaped photothermal evaporator with different array densities by digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technology with thiol-ene click chemistry reactions, using pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) (PETMP) and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) as photothermal materials to achieve integrated molding of the evaporator. Through structural optimization, the 3 × 3 array structure exhibits the best evaporation performance, with an evaporation rate of 1.91 kg m–2 h–1 and an evaporation efficiency of 90.9% at one solar intensity. When used for photocatalytic degradation of dye wastewater, the degradation efficiency of dyes can reach 86%. In addition, using a 3 × 3 array evaporator to treat salt-containing dye wastewater can cause directional salt collection due to the temperature difference between the top and bottom. After 5 complete evaporation and collection cycles, the average salt collection capacity of the evaporator can still be maintained at 0.593 g, with a salt collection rate of 158.34 mg m–2 h–1. This biomimetic photothermal evaporator provides a solution for the recycle and high purification of salt-containing dye wastewater.

title: Dicationic Porous Poly(Ionic Liquid)s with Hydrogen Bond Donors for Efficient Catalytic Conversion of CO2 under Mild Conditions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The formation of cyclic carbonates by coupling CO2 with epoxides offers a practical way of upgrading the surplus CO2 that has accumulated in the atmosphere, and thus helps to mitigate global warming. Because CO2 is intrinsically robust thermodynamically and sluggish kinetically, however, this transformation usually demands harsh conditions. Herein, a family of porous poly(ionic liquid)s denoted bAm-PIL-x (bAm = bis-amide) was constructed by radical copolymerization of an imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer (tVIm-IL) and a quaternary ammonium-based ionic liquid monomer (tQAm-IL) in the presence of N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide as the cross-linker. These polymers combine a moderate specific surface area, pores spanning several size regimes, and a pronounced affinity for CO2, which makes them well suited to both capturing and converting CO2. Applied to the coupling of CO2 with epoxides under solvent-free, metal-free, and cocatalyst-free conditions, bAm-PIL-2 delivered excellent performance at a mild 80 °C and 1.0 bar. The catalyst was readily regenerated and recycled, and it accepted a wide range of epoxide substrates. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations together with in situ infrared spectroscopy were used to probe how the catalyst, the epoxides, and CO2 interact, and on this basis a plausible reaction mechanism for the cycloaddition is proposed. The present findings offer meaningful guidance for designing highly efficient catalysts for CO2 conversion.

title: Promoting Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Oxalic Acid over Co–Cu Dual-Site Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical coreduction of nitrate (NO3–) and oxalic acid to glycine (ENOG) provides a sustainable alternative to conventional glycine production but remains limited by sluggish reactant activation, inefficient C–N coupling, and competing reaction pathways. Herein, a dual-site metal–organic framework, CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu, is developed as an efficient and robust cathode catalyst for ENOG. Operando spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal the cooperative effect of Cu–Co dual sites in promoting OA-to-*C2H2O3 conversion, *NO3 reduction to *NH2OH, *C2H2O3-*NH2OH coupling to *C2H3NO3, and subsequent *C2H3NO3 hydrogenation for selective glycine formation. Moreover, by integrating cathodic ENOG over the CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu catalyst with an anodic glycerol oxidation over the PbO2 catalyst in a two-electrode electrolyzer, we achieve a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 78.3% and a glycine yield rate of 629.3 mmol h−1 g−1, while enabling the gram-scale production of high-purity glycine.

title: Biomimetic Liquid Diodes Across Materials and Scales for Directional Liquid Transfer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The last decade has witnessed remarkable advancements in liquid diode, evolving from fundamental research to cutting-edge applications such as microfluidics, thermal management, and wearable electronics. However, how material characteristics and structural scales mediate liquid transport on liquid diodes has yet to be fully clarified to date. In this study, we develop a Crassula muscosa inspired liquid diode (CMLD) with superior material adaptability and structural scale adaptability spanning three orders of magnitude. Such a liquid diode endows a cross-material, and cross-scale unidirectional liquid transfer from microscale to macroscale. The mechanisms underlying the role of the wettability, viscosity and structure scale in regulating the liquid transfer kinetics including transfer distance, transfer velocity and liquid rectification, are clearly demonstrated. By combining experimental observation, numerical simulation, and building a theoretical retention force model, the liquid transfer and pinning mechanisms governed by asymmetric reentrant structures are systematically elucidated, which enables superior robustness for unidirectional liquid transfer of continuous flows with various flow rates. These results provide a robust framework for coupling material characteristics and structural scales to achieve controllable unidirectional liquid transfer, laying a solid foundation for the practical implementation of liquid diode-based technologies.

title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ/10 and annular features smaller than λ/60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration.

title: Women might have invented language — but not alone
abstract: An eloquent analysis of the origins of human speech suggests that social cohesion, not conflict, drove our use of words.

title: Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Minimizing H2O2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H2O2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H2O2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H2O2 (0.5 mM), with H2O2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination.

title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

title: MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS2-based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS2-based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

title: Author Correction: A decoupling strategy toward spatiotemporal regulation and biomechanical transmission of sandwiched scaffold for osteochondral regeneration
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds

title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5σ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

title: Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam’s potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.

title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d-p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH4 over 1000 mA/cm2. With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH4-rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells.

title: Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
abstract: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Cisplatin Conjugated with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

title: Comparing Nuclear Reaction Coordinates Driving Photoinduced Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.

title: Mechanistic Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Addition
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters. This protocol delivers enantioenriched α-quaternary amino acid derivatives in up to 95% ee, completely circumventing the need for stoichiometric metal reductants. Beyond its synthetic utility, the electrochemical platform uniquely enables the direct interrogation of the operative electron-transfer events. A comprehensive mechanistic study─encompassing cyclic voltammetry, in situ electrochemical EPR spectroscopy, DFT calculations, stoichiometric experiments, and radical-trapping experiments─elucidates a highly orchestrated catalytic manifold. Crucially, we demonstrate that the α-imino ester serves a dual role, acting as both a radical acceptor and a redox-active ligand for the chiral cobalt catalyst. Subsequent cathodic reduction of the resulting cobalt–imine complex generates a key low-valent species that engages the alkyl halide via a turnover-limiting single-electron transfer (SET) to produce the requisite alkyl radical. Overall, this work establishes a robust electrochemical framework that synergizes reaction innovation with fundamental mechanistic elucidation in asymmetric radical catalysis.

title: Aligned Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

title: Regulating carrier transport and oxychloride interphase formation by increasing configurational complexity in solid-state halide electrolytes
abstract: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.

title: Decoding the risks of hydrogels for bone regeneration
abstract: Hydrogels offer adaptable matrices for bone regeneration, yet clinical translation remains limited by application-specific failures in dynamic skeletal environments. This Review organizes these failures into mechanical, spatiotemporal and immune risks and outlines translational benchmarks and risk-controlled design principles.
